facts.claim: Processing of stimuli from both the inside and outside of the body converges primarily in the supramarginal gyrus bilaterally.
facts.quote: Using a multilevel kernel density analysis, we found that processing of stimuli of the two domains converges primarily in the supramarginal gyrus bilaterally.

facts.claim: A right-lateralized set of areas, including the precentral and postcentral, and superior temporal gyri, are candidates to match multiple body-related signals.
facts.quote: Furthermore, we found a right-lateralized set of areas, including the precentral and postcentral, and superior temporal gyri. We discuss these results and propose this set of areas as ideal candidates to match multiple body-related signals

facts.claim: Interactive media is linked to increased time perception compared to non-interactive media.
facts.quote: Results showed reduced agentive involuntariness, but increased flow, presence, character involvement, and time perception for interactive compared to non-interactive media.

facts.claim: Personality traits of openness and conscientiousness are linked to moderate alteration of aspects of self representation during media engagement.
facts.quote: Personality traits of openness and conscientiousness were also associated with moderate alteration of aspects self representation during media engagement.

facts.claim: Absorption is linked to increased flow, presence, and character involvement.
facts.quote: Absorption was associated with increased flow, presence and character involvement.

research.angle: Interactive digital media is linked to increased time perception and altered self-representation, while specific brain regions are involved in integrating internal and external bodily signals.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that interactive media can increase time perception and flow, but it does not specifically confirm that high-frequency consumption distorts neural processing speed.
research.caveat: The study on time perception (S2) used 220 participants and did not specify the frequency or duration of digital consumption.
